t: For purposes of section 503(a)(3) of this Act, up to $15,000,000 may be reprogrammed within “United States Secret Service—Operations and Support”.

fable.w: This provision only authorizes reprogramming of appropriated funds within a Secret Service account. A tempting reading is that reprogramming under section 503 implies notifying congressional committees, but Congress is inside the federal government, and the text mentions no such process in any case. No state, tribe, expert, company, or member of the public is consulted, heard, or given a right to sue.
fable.s: up to $15,000,000 may be reprogrammed within “United States Secret Service—Operations and Support”

qwen_block.w: This section authorizes the internal reprogramming of funds within a specific federal agency's budget. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or input from any parties outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private entities). The decision is made entirely within the executive branch.
qwen_block.s: For purposes of section 503(a)(3) of this Act, up to $15,000,000 may be reprogrammed within “United States Secret Service—Operations and Support”.

opus.w: This section only lets up to $15,000,000 be moved within one Secret Service appropriations account. It involves no states, tribes, experts, companies, or members of the public in any federal decision. The cross-reference to section 503(a)(3) suggests a reprogramming procedure, but any notice under that section would go to congressional committees, which are inside the federal government. So it does not count as participation.
opus.b: The tempting reading is to see "section 503(a)(3)" as a process requirement. In appropriations acts, section 503 usually governs reprogramming and notice to the Appropriations Committees. Even so, the committees are part of Congress, so they are inside the federal government. No outside party is involved.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the reprogramming of federal funds within a specific agency account. It does not require or recommend any consultation, coordination, or participation with parties outside the federal government (such as the public, states, or private entities). The decision-making process described is internal to the federal government's budgetary operations.
qwen_chat.s: For purposes of section 503(a)(3) of this Act, up to $15,000,000 may be reprogrammed within “United States Secret Service—Operations and Support”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that reprogramming funds involves a decision-making process that could theoretically involve outside input, but the text itself is purely an internal budgetary authorization. It does not mention any consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory body involving non-federal entities. The actors involved are implicitly the federal agencies managing the budget (Secret Service, Treasury, OMB, Congress), all of which are inside the federal government.
